en.question: Which change is most likely to reduce spend on a high-volume summarisation service without reducing quality?

options.text: Remove the system prompt entirely to save its tokens on every request.
options.note: Saves very little and usually costs quality, which is a false economy.

options.text: Set temperature to 0 so the model produces a more economical response.
options.note: Sampling temperature has no effect on price.

options.text: Trim input boilerplate, cap output length, and cache the stable prefix.
Disable streaming, since incremental delivery carries a billing overhead.
options.note: Streaming is billed identically to a blocking response.

en.explanation: Spend is tokens in plus tokens out. Those three reduce token volume rather than degrade the task: less input, no output nobody reads, and a discounted rate on the repeated prefix.
